newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo plans to buy Renault's Mack - paper.
newsitem.headline: Volvo plans to buy Renault's Mack - paper.

text.p: Volvo Trucks, a unit of Swedish automotive group AB Volvo, is planning to buy French vehicle maker Renault's North American truck group Mack, a Swedish newspaper said on Tuesday.
"The deal would double Volvo's market share and give it access to Mack's network of retailers and service plants in the U.S.," said daily newspaper Svenska Dagbladet.
Volvo wants to secure at least a 20 percent U.S. market share and currently has a 10 percent holding while Mack has 8.8 percent.
But the newspaper said the deal had complications. Renault would think of selling Mack -- but Volvo would also have to take over Renault's previously troubled European truck operations.
Svenska Dagbladet said Volvo was not interested in doing that.
"A key point is that Volvo's new chief executive in North America, Marc Gustafson, was recruited from Mack and therefore knows the company inside out," the newspaper said.

"In addition, Volvo and Mack were...on their way to merge in connection with the planned merger between Volvo and Renault. The companies have thereby very intimate knowledge of each others' strengths and weaknesses."
Volvo and Renault planned to merge in 1993 but the marriage failed after a Volvo board room revolt.
Volvo still holds 11.4 percent of capital in Renault, worth around 4.8 billion crowns.

Volvo and Mack would complement each other as Mack is relatively strong with its special vehicles on the construction side in northeast U.S., while Volvo's focus is on long-distance, coast-to-coast traffic, the newspaper said.
Mack has also succeeded in having its own engines in its trucks, while Volvo's customers prefer to buy engines from independent U.S. manufacturers.
